findings.title: broker.pid records the CLI's own PID, so shutdown on Windows force-kills the CLI before its own cleanup runs
findings.evidence: local-broker.ts:178 writes `process.pid` (the CLI process that hosts the embedded broker) into `<reportDir>/broker.pid`. The only consumer of `*.pid` files is `killTracked(reportDir)` (process-manager.ts:90-116), which reads every `.pid` file in reportDir and kills that PID. On win32 it runs `taskkill /PID <pid> /F /T`. `setupCleanup` in run-local.ts:221-229 calls `killTracked(reportDir)` first, then `extraCleanup?.()`, `brokerHandle.cleanup()`, `printLogPaths(reportDir)` and `process.exit(exitCode)`. Because broker.pid holds the CLI's own PID, `taskkill /F /T` force-terminates the CLI (and its whole tree) from inside killTracked, so none of the later steps run. On POSIX the self-sent SIGTERM is only queued, and the `cleaningUp` guard plus the synchronous `process.exit` hide the problem. The embedded broker lives in-process and is already stopped by `brokerHandle.cleanup()`, so a PID file for it is wrong in the first place.
findings.impact: On Windows, any `run:local:*` session that started the embedded broker ends with the CLI force-killed: the producer's exit code is replaced by taskkill's forced exit code (so a passing run looks failed in CI or scripts), `extraCleanup` (for example stopping device log capture, run-local.ts:512/619/773) is skipped, and the log-path summary never prints.
findings.reproduction: On Windows, with no MQTT broker running, run a `run:local` command so ensureBroker starts the embedded aedes broker and writes reportDir/broker.pid. Let the producer exit with code 0, or press Ctrl+C. Check `echo %ERRORLEVEL%`: it is non-zero, and the 'log paths' output after 'Shutting down...' is missing.
findings.fix: Don't write the CLI's own PID to a `.pid` file that killTracked reads. Drop the broker.pid write, since `cleanup()` already stops the in-process broker, or give it a name or extension killTracked skips. Another option is for killTracked to skip `pid === process.pid`.
